_meta.description: Visual-similarity grouping for counterfactual (CF) object selection. Single source of truth harmonizing bddl_preprocessor._CF_CATEGORY and scripts/rate_cf_bddls.py:_CATEGORY (WS-4 hardcoding audit). Loaded at runtime; the in-code dicts are fallbacks.
_meta.semantics: Objects sharing a cf_category look similar, so swapping one for another is a WEAK grounding test (a language-blind policy could guess right). CF generation prefers cross-group swaps; rate_cf scores same-group swaps lower on cf_value.
_meta.axis_note: cf_category (visual-grounding similarity) is INTENTIONALLY distinct from physical_category in surface_compatibility.json (placement plausibility). Example: wine_bottle and ketchup are both physical_category=bottle (placement), but cf_category bottle vs food_can (a wine bottle and a ketchup bottle look different). Do not merge the two axes.
harmonization: Adopted the finer-grained labels from the live eval pipeline (bddl_preprocessor._CF_CATEGORY) as canonical: {bowl_plate, bottle, food_can, food_box, mug, book, container}.

rate_cf_bddls.py:_CATEGORY previously lumped all condiments+bottles into one 'bottle' group and all cartons+soup into one 'box' group; harmonizing splits condiments/cans (food_can) from tall bottles (bottle), and soup-cans (food_can) from rectangular cartons (food_box), matching the production partition. This changes rate_cf scoring output only (a non-eval scoring script) — documented intentional difference.
rate_cf labels bowl->bowl_plate and tray->container are pure relabels (same partition).
_meta.coverage: All 34 registry assets are categorized. Entries not present in the historical _CF_CATEGORY (16 entries) are coverage additions; each is justified below. Adding a category to a previously-uncategorized asset can move a CF swap from cross-group (preferred) to same-group (deprioritized) — intended when the two objects are genuinely look-alikes.

additions_justification.chefmate_8_frypan: bowl_plate: shallow open pan, bowl-like profile (rate_cf already grouped it as bowl).
